create.name: Dassanāya Buddhist Community
create.bio:
Dassanāya Buddhist Community is a small non-profit sangha based at a vihara in Alexandria, Virginia, just outside Washington, DC. Its name is a Pāli word meaning roughly 'in order to see', and its teaching rests mainly on early Buddhism and the Pāli discourses, with Zen texts such as the Heart Sutra and Dogen's writings also in the mix. The guiding teacher is Dhammadīpā, also known as Kōnin Melissa Cardenas, who began Zen practice in 1987, trained at Hosshinji in Japan, Tassajara and San Francisco Zen Center, received Dharma transmission in the Shunryu Suzuki line, and spent five years as a Theravāda nun before setting down those precepts in 2024. She is a past president of the Soto Zen Buddhist Association, and the community follows that body's ethics code.

The community runs weekly programmes, including the Sunday Sound of Dhamma series of guided meditation and talk, along with classes, ceremonies, brunches and retreats, open both in person and on Zoom. Dhammadīpā teaches in English and Spanish, reflecting her Colombian heritage, and two community teachers lead further sittings. A large library of talks is free on its YouTube channel and audio pages, and her book on the practice of giving, Gifts Greater Than the Oceans, can be downloaded at no cost.

courses.title: Weekly Programmes, Classes and Retreats
courses.description: The community's calendar of weekly guided meditation and Dharma talks, sutta study, ceremonies and retreats, held at the Alexandria vihara and on Zoom. Everyone is welcome; the community is supported by donations.

free_resources.title: Gifts Greater Than the Oceans: Benefits of the Buddhist Practice of Giving
free_resources.description: Dhammadīpā's 2020 book on dāna, the practice of generosity, offered as a free PDF in English with a Spanish edition also available. Printed copies can be requested.

free_resources.title: English Audio Teachings
free_resources.description: Free recordings of chanting, talks on the Zen bodhisattva precepts and the refuges, and Dharma talks and a guided meditation by Dhammadīpā, with a link to her larger archive on Dharma Seed.

free_resources.title: Video Dhamma
free_resources.description: A page of recorded talks by the guiding teacher on metta, joy, right view, right speech and ethics, plus a six-part class on the Heart Sutra from 2019.
